claims.text: TC4 is a Ti6Al4V alloy with a typical alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
The typical alpha-plus-beta microstructure of TC4 provides good ductility.
Untreated TC4 has low hardness and poor wear or tribological performance under extreme contact stresses.
Multi-energy implantation of Nb and Mo followed by low-temperature nitriding will produce a nanostructured, diffusion-modified surface layer on TC4.
Optimized implantation energies and doses can uniformly modify the near-surface region without exceeding damage thresholds.
Nitriding TC4 at 300–400 degrees Celsius in controlled ammonia can avoid undesired phase transformation.
The treatment will create a surface layer enriched in Nb, Mo, and nitrogen-induced precipitates.
The modified layer will form a graded transition zone with strong metallurgical bonding to the unmodified TC4 substrate.
Refractory-ion implantation introduces controlled defects and changes local surface chemistry.
Implantation-induced defects and modified local chemistry act as nucleation sites during subsequent nitriding.
Low-temperature nitriding incorporates nitrogen and precipitates hard phases within the implanted surface layer.
The engineered layer and its hard precipitates will significantly increase TC4 surface hardness relative to untreated TC4.
The treatment will reduce friction and wear relative to untreated TC4 under high-contact-stress and severe-friction conditions.
The surface treatment will preserve the bulk alloy's ductility, toughness, microstructure, and phase stability.
Performance gains depend on remaining within an optimized implantation and nitriding parameter window.
The uniformity and depth of the modified layer are sensitive to ion-implantation parameters.
